title: Which MySQL to Iceberg tool fits you?

questions.hint: Free software still has a bill: servers and people.

options.label: A vendor runs it for me
options.why: you want a vendor to run it

options.label: My team runs it, with a UI or command line
options.why: you want to self-host, and Fivetran's lake destination runs as SaaS only

options.label: My team runs it, as Java services or code
options.why: you want to self-host, and Fivetran's lake destination runs as SaaS only

options.label: Kafka, and several teams read the changes
Neither, I want few moving parts

questions.q: Where will the Iceberg tables live?

options.label: Google Cloud or Azure storage
options.why: Estuary's Iceberg connector supports only Amazon S3 today

options.label: Not decided yet
options.why: you want a wide choice of storage

questions.q: How do you feel about licences and fees?

options.label: It must have an open-source licence
options.why: Airbyte Core uses the Elastic License 2.0 and Estuary uses the Business Source License

options.label: No licence fee, I will pay for servers
options.why: you want to avoid a licence fee

options.label: I can pay a vendor fee
options.why: you can budget a paid plan

questions.q: What else will you move besides MySQL?

options.label: Many other sources, including SaaS apps
options.why: you need SaaS app sources, which Airbyte and Fivetran cover

debezium.name: Debezium Server with the community Iceberg sink
debezium.summary: Debezium's own MySQL reader without Kafka, writing to Iceberg through a community sink.
debezium.bestWhen: you want Debezium's reader and don't mind running a Java service.
debezium.watchOut: the sink is community maintained and its page lists no catalogs. Upsert is off by default, and compaction is on you.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Free software that copies MySQL into Iceberg tables with a UI or command line, on your own infrastructure.
olake.bestWhen: you want a ready-made job, many catalogs and no licence fee.
olake.watchOut: it runs on your own infrastructure, writes Iceberg and Parquet, and OLake Fusion handles compaction.

kafka.name: Kafka Connect with Debezium and the Iceberg sink
kafka.summary: Debezium reads MySQL into Kafka, and the Iceberg sink writes the topics into tables.
kafka.bestWhen: Kafka is already your backbone and several readers use the same topics.
kafka.watchOut: the Debezium transform is experimental, table creation is off by default, and you run three systems.

flink.name: Flink CDC
flink.summary: A MySQL source and an Iceberg sink in one project, running on Apache Flink.
flink.watchOut: the source table needs a primary key, the sink is at-least-once, and you add the MySQL JDBC driver yourself.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: One tool for MySQL and hundreds of other connectors, with a free self-managed Core and a credit-based Cloud.
airbyte.bestWhen: MySQL is one of many sources you need to move.
airbyte.watchOut: Core is under the Elastic License 2.0, which is not open source, syncs run on a schedule, and the destination does not describe compaction.

fivetran.name: Fivetran Managed Data Lake Service
fivetran.summary: A vendor-run service that keeps your data in your own bucket and handles table upkeep.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want someone else to run it.
fivetran.watchOut: no support for Iceberg position deletes, SaaS only, and priced on monthly active rows.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: Capture and delivery in one product, with MySQL capture and an Iceberg connector that runs Spark jobs.
estuary.bestWhen: you are on AWS and want a vendor to run it.
estuary.watchOut: it needs an EMR Serverless application, an S3 staging bucket and IAM roles, and supports only REST catalogs on Amazon S3 today.

supermetal.name: Supermetal
supermetal.summary: A single self-hosted agent that writes Iceberg V3 or V2 and is priced on compute.
supermetal.bestWhen: you want a lean agent and can budget the fee.
supermetal.watchOut: no data type promotion yet, compaction is on you, and it is paid after the trial and the licence is not stated.
